findings.detail: No protected document changed in this interval. CHARTER.md and AUTHORITY.md are byte-identical across all 25 commits, so no reserved decision — Charter edit, authority edit, grant change, destructive or externally visible act — was taken by the agent. The one governance edit is a90f243 (PR #157) to ARCHITECTURE.md, which is co-owned design rather than a protected document, and its rule is congruence review plus notification rather than authentication: the PR carries the impact, the reasoning and the cost that motivated it, and the direction is the maintainer's instruction of 2026-10-14, quoted verbatim and dated inside the policy text. That amendment widened the agent's own release scope from patch-only to any semver level, and AUTHORITY.md reserves 'widening the agent's own scope' to the maintainer, so the honest reading is that the standing § Release delegation supplied the authority to cut releases while the referenced policy supplied the limit, and moving that limit needed the maintainer. Nothing reserved was exercised: retiring or deleting a tag or release stayed reserved and was not used (v0.3.0 remains tagged and unpublished), and changing the policy stayed reserved. Whether the recorded instruction authenticates the widening is not something this repository can establish, because every GitHub actor here is the same account; that is carried as open_questions[0] rather than presented as a pass on authentication. Watermarking held throughout: every merged PR carries the [yolo] title prefix and the footer plus HTML marker naming its outcome issue, including #157 and #158.

open_questions.question: Does the recorded maintainer instruction authenticate the widening of the agent's release scope in ARCHITECTURE.md?
open_questions.detail: a90f243 moved the versioning policy from patch-only to any semver level, quoting the maintainer's 2026-10-14 instruction verbatim and dating it inside the policy. AUTHORITY.md reserves 'widening the agent's own scope' to the maintainer, so this edit is authority-relevant even though ARCHITECTURE.md is not a protected document. The instruction's only durable artifact is agent-authored text in a shared account, which by this repository's own watermark rule cannot authenticate a human. Under the grant's weaker standard — 'the agent cannot publish as the maintainer without recorded human intent' — the bar is met, and nothing reserved was exercised. The two readings differ, and this repository cannot settle which applies.
open_questions.impact: Affects the standing release delegation's evidentiary basis, not any delivered artifact: v0.4.0 is correct, tagged, published and acceptance-passed either way.
open_questions.cheapest_resolution: One comment from the maintainer, in their own words, confirming the ARCHITECTURE.md versioning clause at c1daf3e. That converts an agent-recorded instruction into an authenticated one and closes this permanently.

open_questions.question: AUTHORITY.md's Release clause both delegates 'create and retire tags and releases' and reserves 'deleting tags or releases'. Which reading governs retirement?
open_questions.detail: The same bullet delegates retirement and then reserves deletion, and the amended policy now states that retiring or deleting stays reserved. Nothing was retired or deleted in this interval — v0.3.0 remains tagged and unpublished — so the conservative reading was applied in practice. The tension is pre-existing and sits in a protected document, so the agent does not resolve it.
open_questions.impact: None observed. It is a latent ambiguity that could be read permissively by a future session.
open_questions.cheapest_resolution: A one-clause edit to AUTHORITY.md stating that retiring or deleting is reserved, which is how the policy already reads.
